title: Intersecting families of permutations with a fixed number of cycles
summary: Let $\mathrm{Sym(n,k)}$ denote the set of permutations on $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ with exactly $k$ cycles. A family $\mathcal{F}\subset\mathrm{Sym}(n,k)$ is said to be intersecting if $σ^{-1}τ$ has a fixed point for all $σ,τ\in\mathcal{F}$. In this paper, we investigate the size and structure of maximum-sized intersecting families of permutations in $\mathrm{Sym}(n,k)$. In the regime $k\leq n^{0.25}$, we show that every maximum-sized intersecting family is a star, meaning it consists of all permutations in $\mathrm{Sym}(n,k)$ that agree at a given point in $[n]$.
